title: Using sorter2r with {targets}
text: sorter2r package provides R wrappers SORTER2 Python pipeline, assembles phases allopolyploid sequences target-capture sequencing data. pipeline runs series computationally intensive steps—SPAdes assembly, read mapping, haplotype phasing—can take hours complete real datasets. {targets} package natural fit: tracks inputs outputs stage re-runs stages whose inputs changed since last successful run, making long pipelines reproducible efficient. vignette walks complete sorter2r pipeline using {targets}.

title: Using sorter2r with {targets}
text: following software must installed running pipeline. Python tools (install conda environment, typically named "SORTER2"): SORTER2 SPAdes (genome assembler) bwa (read mapper) samtools (SAM/BAM utilities) MAFFT (multiple sequence aligner) vsearch usearch (sequence clustering) R packages: Environment variables (optional recommended; avoids repeating conda_env = "SORTER2" every call):
code: install.packages(c("targets", "tarchetypes")) remotes::install_github("joelnitta/sorter2r") Sys.setenv(SORTER2R_CONDA_ENV = "SORTER2")

title: Using sorter2r with {targets}
text: Create _targets.R file project root. pipeline flows linearly: stage reads predecessor’s output directory writes dedicated output directory, ensuring {targets} can detect changes reliably. tar_file() ({tarchetypes}) shorthand tar_target(..., format = "file"). tells {targets} track output directory hashing contents; change directory invalidates target triggers re-run downstream.
code: library(targets) library(tarchetypes) library(sorter2r)  list(   # Input files ----   tar_file(reads_dir, "data/fastq"),   tar_file(ref, "data/reference/sorter2.fasta"),   tar_file(plastome_ref, "data/reference/plastome.fasta"),    # Stage 1A: assemble reads with SPAdes ----   tar_file(     stage1a,     sorter2_stage1a(       reads_dir  = reads_dir,       output_dir = "results/stage1a",       trim       = FALSE,       spades     = TRUE,       conda_env  = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Filter to ingroup assemblies only ----   tar_file(     ingroup_assemblies,     sorter2_filter_assemblies(       input_dir       = stage1a,       output_dir      = "results/stage1a_ingroups",       exclude_samples = c("outgroup_sample1")     )   ),    # Stage 1B: cluster loci ----   tar_file(     stage1b,     sorter2_stage1b(       input_dir  = ingroup_assemblies,       output_dir = "results/stage1b",       ref        = ref,       loci       = 479L,       conda_env  = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Infer hybrid candidates from cluster pattern ----   tar_target(     hybrids,     sorter2_infer_hybrids(stage1b)   ),    # Stage 2: phase orthologs ----   tar_file(     stage2,     sorter2_stage2(       input_assemblies = ingroup_assemblies,       input_clusters   = stage1b,       output_dir       = "results/stage2",       reads_dir        = reads_dir,       threads          = 6L,       conda_env        = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Stage 3: phase hybrids ----   tar_file(     stage3,     sorter2_stage3(       input_phased     = stage2,       input_assemblies = ingroup_assemblies,       output_dir       = "results/stage3",       phaseset_dir     = ingroup_assemblies,       hybrid_samples   = hybrids$sample[hybrids$candidate],       reads_dir        = reads_dir,       ref              = ref,       loci             = 479L,       conda_env        = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Summarize progenitor sequences ----   tar_file(     progenitor_res,     sorter2_progenitor_processor(       input_dir  = file.path(         stage3, "phaseset", "diploidclusters_phased"       ),       output_dir = "results/progenitor",       mapfile    = "data/reference/progenitor_map.csv",       outgroups  = "data/reference/outgroups.txt",       conda_env  = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Processor: filter and summarize final alignments ----   tar_file(     processor_res,     sorter2_processor(       input_dir  = stage1b,       output_dir = "results/processor",       conda_env  = "SORTER2"     )   ),    # Hapl-O-Miner: recover organellar sequences ----   tar_file(     haplominer_res,     sorter2_haplominer(       input_dir       = stage1a,       output_dir      = "results/haplominer",       organellar_ref  = plastome_ref,       reads_dir       = reads_dir,       threads         = 6L,       clean_workfiles = TRUE,       conda_env       = "SORTER2"     )   ) )

title: sorter2r
text: sorter2r R package wraps core SORTER2 Python scripts. initial implementation thin design: validates arguments, constructs CLI calls, executes original Python entry points.

title: sorter2r
text: sorter2_format_reads() sorter2_stage1a() sorter2_stage1b() sorter2_stage2() sorter2_stage3() sorter2_processor()

title: sorter2r
text: function takes explicit input output directory arguments, forming linear pipeline step’s output feeds next. Stage 2 takes two inputs (Stage 1A Stage 1B outputs); Stage 3 also takes two inputs (Stage 2 Stage 1A outputs). Set dry_run = TRUE call preview command without running . Set SORTER2R_CONDA_ENV avoid repeating conda_env every call:
code: library(sorter2r)  # Optional: rename raw FASTQ files according to a sample map CSV sorter2_format_reads(   input     = "samples.csv",   reads_dir = "raw_reads/" )  # Stage 1A — trim (optional) and/or assemble contigs with SPAdes. # Set trim = FALSE if reads are already cleaned; pass reads_dir to # sorter2_stage2() in that case so Stage 2 can locate the FASTQ files. sorter2_stage1a(   reads_dir  = "raw_reads/",   output_dir = "results/stage1a/",   trim       = TRUE,   spades     = TRUE,   conda_env  = "SORTER2" )  # Stage 1B — cluster assembled contigs into ortholog groups sorter2_stage1b(   input_dir  = "results/stage1a/",   output_dir = "results/stage1b/",   ref        = "reference/baits.fasta",   loci       = 100,   conda_env  = "SORTER2" )  # Stage 2 — phase bi-allelic haplotypes # input_assemblies: Stage 1A output (*_assembly/ dirs) # input_clusters:   Stage 1B output (diploidclusters/ and diploids/) # reads_dir:        directory with raw FASTQ files (*_R1.fastq / *_R2.fastq). #   Required when Stage 1A was run with trim = FALSE (pre-cleaned reads). #   Omit when trim = TRUE — reads are already inside the *_assembly/ dirs. sorter2_stage2(   input_assemblies = "results/stage1a/",   input_clusters   = "results/stage1b/",   output_dir       = "results/stage2/",   reads_dir        = "raw_reads/",   conda_env        = "SORTER2" )  # Stage 3 — phase hybrid loci # phaseset_dir: where to find hybrid *_assembly/ dirs (usually Stage 1A output). #   The wrapper copies them into output_dir/phaseset/ automatically. # hybrid_samples: names of hybrid samples to copy; omit to copy all *_assembly/. sorter2_stage3(   input_phased     = "results/stage2/",   input_assemblies = "results/stage1a/",   output_dir       = "results/stage3/",   phaseset_dir     = "results/stage1a/",   hybrid_samples   = c("Sample1_species", "Sample2_species"),   ref              = "reference/baits.fasta",   loci             = 100,   conda_env        = "SORTER2" )  # Processor — filter and summarise final outputs sorter2_processor(   input_dir  = "results/stage3/",   output_dir = "results/processed/",   conda_env  = "SORTER2" ) Sys.setenv(SORTER2R_CONDA_ENV = "SORTER2")

title: Identify candidate hybrid or polyploid samples from Stage 1B output — sorter2_infer_hybrids
text: Reads consensus-allele summary table produced sorter2_stage1b() computes per-sample allele-count statistics useful distinguishing diploids hybrids polyploids. Polyploids carry extra genome copies, total consensus-allele count across loci proportionally elevated relative diploids.

title: Identify candidate hybrid or polyploid samples from Stage 1B output — sorter2_infer_hybrids
code: sorter2_infer_hybrids(input_dir, min_mean = 2)

title: Identify candidate hybrid or polyploid samples from Stage 1B output — sorter2_infer_hybrids
text: input_dir Directory containing Stage 1B output. Must contain diploids/ subdirectory file matching ALLsamples_consensusallele_*_SUMMARY_TABLE.csv. min_mean Minimum mean consensus alleles per locus required flag sample hybrid/polyploid candidate. Default 2.0: samples average two allele copies per locus flagged.

title: Identify candidate hybrid or polyploid samples from Stage 1B output — sorter2_infer_hybrids
text: data frame one row per sample, sorted descending mean_per_locus, columns: sample Sample name (trailing _ stripped; matches names accepted hybrid_samples argument sorter2_stage3()). total_alleles Sum consensus alleles across loci. n_loci Number loci least one consensus allele. mean_per_locus total_alleles / n_loci. Primary ploidy proxy: diploids typically show 1–2; values 2 suggest polyploidy. candidate TRUE mean_per_locus >= min_mean.

title: Identify candidate hybrid or polyploid samples from Stage 1B output — sorter2_infer_hybrids
text: Interpretation guidance (SORTER2 documentation, full-dataset scale): Diploids: ~1–2 consensus alleles per locus average Tetraploids: ~2–3 per locus Hexaploids: ~4+ per locus Note absolute counts depend number loci analysed; use mean_per_locus cross-dataset comparisons rather total_alleles. complete hybrid assessment, combine allele-count statistics ADMIXTURE ancestry proportions phylogenetic placement.
